A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STRIDE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original protein-fluorescence and molecular-editing experiments, baseline comparisons, reward curves, and appendix analyses of editing interfaces and off-target property changes.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds AAV evaluation, specialist comparisons, attribution and execution tests, iterative refinement, SELFIES results, and backbone comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix E adds closed-loop inference that feeds the best executed candidate into the next round, and a SELFIES-input SFT variant. The core atomic-edit semantics, Levenshtein supervision, and SFT/RL objectives remain unchanged. Renaming the trace and expanding the explanation of already evaluated GSPO/CISPO variants do not themselves establish algorithm changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds FLIP AAV capsid viability/packaging evaluation, extending protein coverage beyond GFP fluorescence to a different protein family and biological function. The original GFP and MEGA-MolEdit/DrugAssist coverage remains; the six DrugAssist task families in Appendix E.5 overlap existing molecular tasks.

E2.justification: New reported comparisons include EVOLVEpro on GFP/AAV, GGS on GFP-TAPE, and DrugAssist on six molecular task families (Tables 9, 10, and 13). DrugAssist previously supplied evaluation data but was not an evaluated comparator. The original GFP and molecular comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include EVOLVEpro's 10 rounds of 16 queries with ground-truth activity metrics, gap-specific GGS top-128 evaluation, mutation-count execution tests, and fixed-budget 90-candidate refinement schedules. Additional backbone and representation configurations are evaluated. The original 100-candidate protein protocol, 500-by-14 molecular evaluation, and Appendix C training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 and Appendix E add attribution tests separating direct generation, structured edits without rationale, and full STRIDE; execution reliability across edit horizons; closed-loop schedule comparisons; SELFIES analysis; and cross-backbone tests. These substantially extend the retained R-group/index-level and off-target-drift analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly reports five-seed EVOLVEpro averages with plus/minus values and four-seed GGS means. The authors' EVOLVEpro comparison uses an explicitly single-run LLM sampler. Statistical reporting therefore expands locally, without adding uncertainty estimates throughout the main experiments; the existing training seed of 42 is retained.

E6.justification: Tables 4 and 9–14 add substantial results, including AAV outcomes, specialist comparisons, and exact execution of 95/100 versus 26/100 in the short- and longer-horizon tests. Original result tables otherwise retain their numerical values, except Table 3 corrects STRIDE uniqueness from 78/79 to 78/89. Figure 2 also changes the plotted reward trajectories; the PDFs do not establish these as same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The Levenshtein recurrence, executable-index definitions, SFT/GRPO objectives, reward formulas, and Appendix A Edit Flows mathematics are retained. Generalizing the protein scorer notation to cover AAV introduces no substantive new mathematical reasoning, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central executable-edit and two-stage training contributions remain. The abstract now explicitly bounds the protein headline to an oracle-based full-action stress test and the molecular claim to GSPO versus STRIDE-SFT. The conclusion adds AAV and closed-loop applicability while dropping the earlier emphasis on strongest gains in long-horizon settings.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of attribution, transfer, representation, and backbone results, alongside protein-GRPO mode collapse and quantified long-horizon failure. It removes the ProtParam shortcut discussion and foregrounds the already existing oracle limitation. Some new interpretations overreach: Appendix E.5 claims SELFIES is strongest on HBD, although Table 13 gives SMILES-GSPO higher strict success.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies reasoning-region serialization and resolves Appendix D's denominator placeholder to valid outputs, consistent with the existing main-text definition. It also documents specialist implementations, including ESM2/random-forest components and GGS filtering and smoothing settings. The main training hyperparameter lists and code-access address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The central research positioning remains, with added context from Block Diffusion, ESM, DeepSeek-R1, AAV/FLIP, EVOLVEpro, GGS, and SELFIES. The DPO discussion/reference and Langley reference are removed. Updates to existing works' titles, venues, and bibliographic details are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, contribution bullets, discussion, conclusion, and impact statement; changes the acronym expansion to Iterative Discrete Editing; and relabels think traces as edit trajectories. It adds Appendix E and a conflict disclosure, while preserving the main section order and much of the technical exposition.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn as a four-panel workflow. Figure 2 becomes a wider three-panel display, adding a success-versus-shift plot of existing results. Seven new tables present the added studies, while retained tables receive relocation, caption, and formatting changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the limited validation of transfer and execution reliability in v1 through AAV evaluation, specialist comparisons, attribution tests, and explicit horizon/backbone failures. Better-qualified headline claims and corrected reporting further improve credibility. These gains outweigh localized problems: specialist uncertainty reporting remains uneven, and the claim of GSPO validity uniformly above 0.90 contradicts Table 13's 0.788 permeability result.
